title: Continuous collector synchronization regression and fairness remediation plan
creator: Miguel Herrera
description: Summary: A production regression introduced in runtime-1.21 caused intermittent breakdowns in the continuous request collector's synchronization path. Symptoms included multi-second tail spikes, temporary starvation of lower-priority traffic (fair-share inversion), and a small number of customer requests timing out during peak traffic windows. This ticket tracks the diagnosis, immediate mitigations, and prioritized long-term remediations to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-07 09:12 UTC - Alert: p95 generation latency on sv-hosting-prod exceeded 1.8s. Alert route: batcher-latency-p95-prod.
2026-03-07 09:18 UTC - Ops triage: observed 'collector-sync' stall on three serving nodes causing batch formation delays. Traffic rerouted to backup pool; partial auto-roll-back triggered.
2026-03-07 09:29 UTC - Mitigation: increased max-window-ms for affected shards and enabled degraded mode to bypass soft-waits; tail latency decreased to baseline by 09:34.

2026-03-07 11:20 UTC - Post-incident debug: kernel change in runtime-1.21 (PR #7643) altered the collector's timer-handling path. Under certain inter-arrival patterns the collector could hold a lock while awaiting an internal readiness flag, blocking lower-priority enqueues.
2026-03-08 - Reproduced locally against a synthetic traffic pattern; added additional telemetry to measure lock hold times and enqueue distribution across priority tiers.
2026-03-09 - Created ticket ENG-100201 to drive remediation work and follow-ups. Assigned initial owners and action items.
2026-03-12 - Deployed patch (PR #7702) to add bounded wait with exponential backoff and a fairness shim; running extended canary in us-west-2.
2026-03-13 - Canary results: tail latency p99 improved but fairness regression remains under specific bimodal load. Further changes required to the priority arbitration algorithm.
2026-03-14 - Next steps agreed in on-call handover and engineering sync.
impact: Approximately 0.6% of requests across 4 customers experienced >2s tail latency during the 22-minute window. No data loss. Two customers reported sporadic client-side timeouts leading to degraded UX in production systems. Estimated revenue/customer impact: low-medium; SLA not breached but user experience affected for a subset of requests.
root_cause: A change to the runtime timing kernel altered collector timer wake semantics. Under a bimodal arrival distribution (bursty high-priority flow mixed with sporadic low-priority background requests) the collector could enter a blocking path while waiting on an internal readiness flag. The blocking path held the collector lock for longer than expected, preventing lower-priority items from being batched and causing both tail latency spikes and fairness inversion.
detection: Detection was triggered by p95/p99 latency alerts. Initial signals included prolonged lock hold durations visible in newly-added debug histograms and a skew in per-priority enqueue counts. Synthetic load reproductions confirmed the inter-arrival pattern required to trigger the regression.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Increased collector max-window-ms and enabled degraded non-blocking enqueue mode as a temporary fallback. 2) Rolled back the most recent runtime kernel tweak for the affected service class on the regional pool. 3) Notified affected customers with targeted status updates. 4) Turned on additional telemetry for lock hold time and per-priority queue depth.
